blocks.text: JavaScript Array flatMap()
ES2019 added the Array flatMap() method to JavaScript.

The flatMap() method first maps all elements of an array
and then creates a new array by flattening the array.

const myArr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];

const newArr = myArr.flatMap(x => [x, x * 10]);

JavaScript Array.from()
The Array.from() method returns an Array object from:

items: Any object with a length property

blocks.text:
let text = "ABCDEFG";

Array.from(text);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
Array.from() has an optional parameter which allows you to execute a function
on each element of the new array:

const myNumbers = [1,2,3,4];

const myArr = Array.from(myNumbers, (x) => x * 2);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The entries() method returns an Array Iterator object with key/value pairs:

The entries() method does not change the original array.
JavaScript Array with() Method
ES2023 added the Array with() method as a safe way to update elements in an array without altering the original array.

const months = ["Januar", "Februar", "Mar", "April"];

const myMonths = months.with(2, "March");
blocks.caption: Example
